repairs.text: Strongest feature: Hernandez clearly connects the proposed nonphysical nature of the soul to a metaphysical method, explaining why conceptual analysis must supplement physical investigation when direct detection is unavailable and keeping his opening responsive to the motion. Principal limitation: His claim that science has virtually nothing to say is too sweeping, because a soul that animates, controls, or otherwise affects a body could generate observable consequences open to indirect empirical comparison. Live burden: He must separate science's inability directly to observe immaterial substance from the stronger exclusion of evidence capable of discriminating embodied-soul explanations from wholly physical rivals. Locked score: The locked score of 69 reflects lucid, motion-responsive framing, but its unsupported empirical boundary overreaches and supplies no positive reason to conclude that a soul exists.

Strongest feature: Hernandez identifies genuine underdetermination by separating agreed observations from metaphysical conclusions, preventing correlations between brains and conscious states from being treated as an automatic verdict that consciousness is wholly physical. Principal limitation: He declares the views empirically equivalent without comparing their expected observations, explanatory commitments, or interaction effects, so his universal claim that no empirical datum could favor either ontology is asserted rather than established. Live burden: He must demonstrate that an embodied-soul account and physical production account predict the same evidence across brain injury, neural stimulation, divided processing, altered awareness, and any proposed bodily interaction. Locked score: The locked score of 72 reflects coherent interpretive caution and direct relevance, while withholding stronger credit because the crucial empirical-equivalence premise receives no comparative defense.
